criteria: A platform whose `buildPath` uses Windows separators (`\`) builds and cleans the same output paths as the identical config using `/`; no doubled or stray separators appear in the paths used or reported.
A `buildPath` with no trailing separator behaves the same as one with a trailing separator, for either separator style, in both build and clean.
Cleaning a platform whose `buildPath` or file `destination` uses `\` removes the built files and prunes the emptied directories, exactly as the equivalent `/` config does.
Neither building nor cleaning raises an error for a `buildPath` that uses `\` separators or omits the trailing separator.
description:
Path handling for `platform.buildPath` is separator-sensitive: logic that joins `buildPath` with a file `destination`, and that prunes the directories left behind after a clean, only recognizes `/`. The historical trailing-separator guard (`buildPath.slice(-1) !== '/'`) likewise only recognized `/`, so a valid Windows-style `buildPath` ending in `\` was rejected with "Build path must end in a trailing slash or you will get weird file names." even though it did end in a separator.

Expected: `/` and `\` are interchangeable everywhere `buildPath` is used, and a `buildPath` works with or without a trailing separator, consistently across both the build (format/write) and clean code paths. A config using `\` separators must produce and clean exactly the same paths as the equivalent `/` config.

Root cause: joining `buildPath` with `destination` via a posix join strips a trailing `/` but keeps a trailing `\` as part of the segment, so backslash-normalization then yields a doubled separator; directory pruning splits and rejoins on `/` only. The build path already normalizes to posix separators (`path-unified/posix` `join` plus backslash normalization) and is the reference behavior the clean path should match.
